note: Executable cross-language verifier parity cases. Private signing keys are intentionally omitted.
mustAssert: Besides `ok`, assert every optional field present on a case: signers, reasonIncludes, reason (the exact refusal text, with API names rewritten per api-name-hints.json), delegatedTo, delegatedQuorum, actionPatterns, verificationLevel, properties, witnessTimes, total, contentVerified, commitmentOnly, brokenAt, unchained, verifiedCount. Bundle options may carry rekorSubmitterKeyIds (map to the pinned Rekor submitter keys); a policy may carry maxAnchorLagSeconds. An approval case's expected.resolverOmitted means a DID-mode anchor over the approverDids keys with no resolver at all. The delegation section runs the delegation (seal) verifier with a DID-mode anchor built from expected.approverDids.

dewpEvidenceHardening.note: DEWP evidence-verifier hardening (Sep 2026 review). Keys are this section's own. Harness as for `bundles`/`evidence`, except: a case's `policy` applies only when present; evidence options may carry `trustedCheckpoints` (caller-trusted checkpoint records) and `rekorKeyId`; single-proof options may carry `trustedCheckpoint`.

verifierInputHardening.note: Verifier input hardening (2026-09-27 review L15-L18, I7, I8). Keys are this section's own. Each sub-section has the shape of the top-level section of the same name and runs with the same harness, except that a bundle case's `policy` applies only when present (as in `dewpEvidenceHardening`). Approval/platform options may carry requireUserVerification and allowOffline.

executionEvidence.note: DEWP §4.7 execution evidence (version 1.1, after the pre-publication review). `cases` are evidence bundles: run each with trustedRoots, evidencePolicy (whose keys may be bare SPKI strings or {key, notBefore?, notAfter?} — DEWP §4.7.5), signaturePolicy, now (evaluation time), skewSeconds, maxWindowSeconds and requireExecutionConfirmed as given; a case with `policy` carries a Rekor-witnessed anchor in its checkpoint and pins the log key in options.rekorSpki (pass it as the anchor policy and the Rekor external key). Then assert ok, execution.byNonce statuses, the per-statement checks (seq, status, trusted) in bundle order, each key of execution.findings that is present (lateContradicted, dispatchConflicts, windowCapped per nonce, sources continuity) and, where present, the per-entry signature checks. `proofs` are single inclusion proofs; `execution` is the expected statement check or null. `statements` are statement-parser cases; `builder` pins the canonical statement bytes. `trustFiles` are SDK cases for the `intyga-evidence-sources` trust-file loader (docs/API.md §2e): parse `text`; an `ok` case must load and yield `policy` — source → keys in file order, each a bare SPKI string or {key, notBefore?, notAfter?} exactly as given — and a refused one must fail to load. Verifier ports may ignore this subsection.

enrolledDevice.note: DIV §4.3.2 enrolled approver devices. Own keys. An approval case's expected.enrolledDeviceKeyIds maps through this section's keys (spkiB64) to expected.enrolledDeviceKeys; a literal expected.enrolledDeviceKeys is passed verbatim. Delegation and agentAuthority cases use a DID-mode anchor from expected.approverDids.
